fields.claim_quote:
We define a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] on $\left({\C^2, \times}\right)$ by:
:$\forall \mathbf a = \tuple {a_1, a_2} \in \C^2: \norm {\mathbf a} = \sqrt {a_1^2 + a_2^2}$

This is a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] because:

:$(1): \quad \norm {\mathbf x} = 0 \iff \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$
fields.explanation: The source formula explicitly squares complex coordinates without conjugates. The main quaternion norm theorem is not refuted. Keep(1,i):sumofsquares0, square-root0, vectornonzero. Actual complex numbers, Complex.I, Complex.sqrt and product vector type.
fields.flaw: The formula sqrt(a_1^2+a_2^2) defines a norm on C^2, in particular satisfying norm(x)=0 iff x=0.
fields.problem:
Title: Quaternions form Algebra

The [[Definition:Quaternion|set of quaternions]] $\Bbb H$ forms an [[Definition:Algebra over Field|algebra]] over the [[Definition:Field of Real Numbers|field of real numbers]].

This [[Definition:Algebra over Field|algebra]] is:
:$(1): \quad$ An [[Definition:Associative Algebra|associative algebra]], but '''not''' a [[Definition:Commutative Algebra (Abstract Algebra)|commutative algebra]].
:$(2): \quad$ A [[Definition:Normed Division Algebra|normed division algebra]].
:$(3): \quad$ A [[Definition:Nicely Normed Star-Algebra|nicely normed $*$-algebra]].
fields.source_context:
0042 | As $\times$ is [[Definition:Commutative Operation|commutative]] on $\C$, it follows that $\tuple {1, 0} \times \tuple {x_1, x_2} = \tuple {x_1, x_2}$.
0043 | 
0044 | So $\tuple {1, 0} \in \C^2$ functions as a [[Definition:Unit of Algebra|unit]].
0045 | 
0046 | That is, $\tuple {\C^2, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Unitary Algebra|unitary algebra]].
0047 | 
0048 | <!--
0049 | From [[Inverses for Complex Multiplication]], every element of $\struct {\C, \times}$ except $0$ has a [[Definition:Multiplicative Inverse|multiplicative inverse]].
0050 | 
0051 | So $\struct {\C, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Division Algebra|division algebra]] and hence a [[Definition:Unitary Division Algebra|unitary division algebra]].
0052 | -->
0053 | 
0054 | We define a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] on $\left({\C^2, \times}\right)$ by:
0055 | :$\forall \mathbf a = \tuple {a_1, a_2} \in \C^2: \norm {\mathbf a} = \sqrt {a_1^2 + a_2^2}$
0056 | 
0057 | This is a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] because:
0058 | 
0059 | :$(1): \quad \norm {\mathbf x} = 0 \iff \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$
0060 | :$(2): \quad \norm {\lambda \mathbf x} = \size \lambda \norm x$
0061 | :$(3): \quad \norm {x - y} \le \norm {x - z} + \norm {z - y}$
0062 | 
0063 | It also follows that:
0064 | :$\norm {x \times y} = \size {x \times y} = \size x \times \size y = \norm x \times \norm y$
0065 | and so $\struct {\C^2, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Normed Division Algebra|normed division algebra]].
0066 |
fields.witness: Take x=(a₁,a₂)=(1,i) ∈ ℂ². Then a₁²+a₂²=1²+i²=1+(-1)=0, so the stated formula gives norm(x)=sqrt(0)=0. However x≠(0,0), since its first coordinate is 1≠0.
